rationale: The literature on biallelic SGSM3 pathogenic variants currently characterizes the disorder as a nonsyndromic or mild-to-moderate intellectual disability phenotype. In cohorts reported to date (Birnbaum et al. in Ashkenazi Jewish families and Turkyilmaz et al. in two siblings with a homozygous stop-gain variant), affected individuals present predominantly with cognitive impairment and short stature without systemic organ malformations. None of the reports describe major structural congenital heart defects, renal anomalies, sensorineural hearing loss, or progressive neurodegenerative regression. Consequently, the presence of these prominent structural or degenerative features serves as an exclusionary/negative criterion arguing against SGSM3-related intellectual developmental disorder autosomal recessive 84 (MRT84). However, overall confidence is bounded by the small total number of reported cases.

evidence.text: Turkyilmaz et al. identified a novel homozygous stop-gain variant (NM_015705.6: c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) in two siblings presenting with intellectual disability and short stature, characterizing SGSM3 as a candidate gene for a nonsyndromic intellectual disability phenotype.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: The report of two cases with bi-allelic LOF variants in the SGSM3 gene from different populations with similar clinical manifestations strengthens the potential of this gene as a candidate gene for the nonsyndromic ID phenotype.

evidence.text: Birnbaum et al. originally delineated an intellectual disability condition associated with a homozygous founder variant in SGSM3 among Ashkenazi Jewish individuals, characterized by autosomal recessive mild to moderate intellectual disability without reports of major congenital visceral malformations.

source.title: Intellectual disability syndrome associated with a homozygous founder variant in SGSM3 in Ashkenazi Jews

new_directions.question_text: Does extended phenotypic characterization across larger multi-ethnic cohorts reveal occult organ system involvement or sensory deficits in SGSM3 loss-of-function carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Only a limited number of individuals across two primary studies have been detailed in the literature; formal systemic screening (audiology, echocardiography, renal ultrasound) across larger international cohorts is required to confirm whether these negative criteria hold uniformly.
